summary:
ADVERSARIAL VERIFICATION OF THE "OPERATIONS" AUDIT (variant 5). Outputs are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-snt-2b-adam-cieniewicz/4246b01c-1857-5934-aed2-b3eb85d88a07/scratchpad/audit/verif_operations/: repro.py, beh.py, marg.py, kcal.py, sub.py, sub_margin.py, funds_chk.py, margin_recomputed_summary.csv, margin_spot_dates.csv, margin_k_calibration_cme.csv, margin_B_ewm_only_daily.csv, funds_recheck.csv and sources_used.csv. No project file was modified.

IMPORTANT LIMITATION: the session's WebSearch budget was already used up (200 of 200), so no new web searches were possible. External facts were checked another way:
- CME historical maintenance margins for GC, SI, HG, CL, ZC, ZS, 6E, 6J and ZN, 2020-06 to 2026-06, transcribed from CME's margin PDFs in a public GitHub dataset (pranavrevuri/margin-event-study).
- Raw Yahoo front-month futures prices (mastermindx-market-intelligence/macro).
- Third-party GitHub fund catalogues (bpineau/pofo, simonesassi-eng/tarzan, madebymlai/aegis and others).
All of these are secondary sources of medium reliability.

1) REPRODUCTION. I reran variant 5 independently: Sharpe 1.1707, vol 21.4%, max drawdown (excess) −54.0% on 2025-05-15. This matches exactly.

2) BEHAVIOUR STATISTICS: essentially all confirmed. Two small notes:
- The yearly figures quoted (2023 −10.5%, 2024 −14.3%, ...) are total returns. The excess-return figures are worse: 2023 −15.0%, 2024 −18.6%, 2025 −2.2%, 2026 YTD −4.0%.
- The total-return max drawdown is −47.6% to −47.8%, depending on how the T-bill is accrued.
Fund comparisons from 2022-09-30 to 2026-07-10 are confirmed: SG Trend +2.6%, DBMF +13.8%, AQMIX +33.8%, KMLM −16.4%, the 20-market subset +17.7%. DBMF's CAGR (9.2%), Sharpe (0.55) and max drawdown (−20.4%) are also confirmed.

3) MARGIN
- The model B and model A numbers reproduce exactly.
- The CME data supports the structure of model B: margin ≈ k × vol × notional, with k stable around 0.24-0.28 over 2020-2026.
- Two individual margin rates were wrong:
  - Gold: 9% is wrong for mid-2026. It was a peak from February to early March 2026; on 2026-06-30 initial margin was about 5.5% of notional.
  - Crude (CL): about 12.3% initial on 2026-06-30, not 9.5%.
- Correcting the class k values barely changes the result: mean 20.0% (unchanged), max 45.6% instead of 47.3%.
- The bigger issue is how the model measures volatility. It uses the larger of 32-day EWMA vol and 1-year vol. The 2009-09-16 peak of 47% comes from the 1-year leg: equity 1-year vol was 42% against 19% for the EWMA. Using the 32-day EWMA alone gives mean 16.7%, p95 25.7%, max 33%.
- The stress test (margin doubled plus the next 5 days' loss) holds the 5-day book fixed. It ignores how fast the system cuts exposure itself (gross exposure fell from 13.4× to 3.5× between 9 and 13 March 2023). It is also partly double counting, because model B margin already rises with volatility.
  - Recomputed day by day, the SVB stress is 76%, not 91%.
  - With EWMA-only margins, the worst stress is about 70%.
  - None of these cases reaches IBKR maintenance-margin liquidation (that requires an initial-margin ratio above about 110%).
- The suggestion that the March 2023 losses were data artefacts is refuted. Raw prices show palladium +8.43% and silver +6.96% on 2023-03-13; the losses were real.

4) UCITS FUNDS. Several material corrections:
- LU2951555403 is the R EUR unhedged class (ticker DBMFE), not R USD. Three independent sources agree. The USD class is LU2951555585 (DBMF on Euronext Paris).
- "The only managed-futures UCITS ETF" is refuted: the BNP Paribas Easy Managed Futures UCITS ETF (LU3307218399, TER 0.60%) launched on 29 May 2026. It is tiny and swap-based.
- The AQR Managed Futures UCITS fund is missing from the list, and it is the closest UCITS equivalent to the user's own trend system.
  - Classes: RAE LU1662502183, IAET LU1662498721, IAE1FT LU2622190622 (1.26% flat), A USD LU1103257975.
  - Fees: 0.6% plus a 10% performance fee, or 1.0% flat, plus a 0.18-0.25% expense cap.
  - Minimum investment: about 100k, which can be waived.
- Confirmed ISINs: Man AHL Trend Alternative LU0424370004 (DNY H EUR), Candriam FR0010794792, Schroder GAIA BlueTrend LU1293073745 (A Acc EUR Hedged).
- Not verified: Winton IE00BG382P13 (the class I could find is IE00BG382Q20, I GBP), Aspect IE00B3Q12S92 (the fund itself exists, synthetic via a total return swap), and the hedged class MFEH's Euronext Paris listing of 2026-09-21. A pofo note written about August 2026 said MFEH was "Xetra only, not yet registered for sale in France".
- PFU 31.4% is confirmed by an independent source.

checked.claim: Stress test (margin x2 plus the realised next-5-day loss): max 96% of equity (Sept 2009), p99 77%
checked.evidence: Numerically reproduced (0.964 on 2009-09-17), but conservative for two reasons. (b) Model B margin already rises with vol. A dynamic 1-day version (2 x yesterday's book margin / equity after today's P&L) gives max 95% (2009-09-21, the 1-year-vol artefact) and p99 76%. With EWMA32-only margins: max 69-71%, p99 57-58%.

checked.claim: SVB, March 2023: margin 37%, drawdown -19.3%, about 91% of equity if exchanges had doubled margins

The wording 'just above maintenance' is misleading: an initial-margin ratio of 91% is a maintenance ratio of about 83%, so there would be no liquidation.

problems: The WebSearch budget for the session was used up (200 of 200) before this verifier started, so no fresh web searches were possible. External facts were checked against secondary GitHub-hosted data: CME margin history transcribed from CME PDFs, raw Yahoo futures prices, and third-party fund catalogues. Treat the fund facts as medium confidence until checked on justETF, the AMF GECO register and broker product search.

The gold margin input (9% of notional) is stale. It was the Feb-Mar 2026 peak; on 2026-06-30 CME gold initial margin was about 5.5% (maintenance $20,115). Crude is understated: about 12.3% initial ($8,550), not 9.5%. 6E is overstated ($2,640, not $2,970). The agent mixed maintenance and initial margins (ZS $2,200 is maintenance; ZN $2,062 is initial). The class k values for metals (0.34) and energy (0.21) are therefore off, although the effect on total margin/equity is small (mean unchanged at 20.0%, max 47.3% → 45.6%).

The model B peak (47% on 2009-09-16) is driven by the 1-year-vol leg of max(EWMA32, 1y), which still contained Q4-2008 equity volatility (1y vol 0.42 against EWMA 0.19). With EWMA32-only margins the max is 33% and the mean 16.7%. The report should give a range, not a single peak.

The stress test (2x margin plus the next-5-day loss) assumes a static book. It ignores the system's own fast de-levering (gross exposure 13.4x → 3.5x in three trading days in March 2023) and partly double counts, since model B already scales with volatility. The SVB 91% figure is an upper bound; recomputed day by day it is about 76%. 'Close to forced liquidation' is overstated: IBKR liquidates on maintenance margin, i.e. an initial-margin ratio of about 110% or more.

The claim that the March 2023 losses may be data artefacts is wrong. Palladium +8.4% and silver +7.0% on 2023-03-13 are confirmed by independent raw prices. The -10.6% day is a genuine consequence of about 10x gross leverage concentrated in short rates.

The previous agent took UCITS share-class identities from unreliable sources. LU2951555403 is the EUR unhedged class (DBMFE), not R USD (that class is LU2951555585). The claim that iMGP DBi is the only managed-futures UCITS ETF is false: BNP Paribas Easy Managed Futures, LU3307218399, launched in May 2026. The AQR Managed Futures UCITS fund, the most relevant direct time-series momentum vehicle, is missing.

The yearly returns in the behaviour summary (2023 -10.5%, 2024 -14.3%, ...) are total returns but sit next to excess-return counts. In excess terms, 2023 is -15.0% and 2024 -18.6%. The labelling should be fixed.
Minor date inconsistency: KMLM's CAGR (7.4%) in alternatives_ucits.csv is measured to 2026-10-01, while the other comparisons stop at 2026-07-10 (KMLM 5.7% to that date).

The workload contract table (contracts.csv) uses full-size contracts where smaller ones exist (ICE Mini FTSE GBP1, Euronext Mini CAC EUR1, Eurex Micro-SMI, OSE Nikkei micro, CME micro ags). As a result, small-capital diversification is slightly understated. Historical notionals are rebased on excess-return indices rather than actual prices, which is approximate (not re-verified in detail).

Back-adjusted prices are only valid as real prices on the last row: the back-adjusted CL1 sits about $20 below actual WTI in 2025. Any historical %-of-notional calculation must not use them. The agent's calibration correctly used 2026 only.
